summary: David Schaberg is a scholar in sinology. He studied at Stanford University (~1982–1986) and Harvard University (~1989–1996), and took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1996.

David Seyfort Ruegg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at EPHE and the University of Paris (~1953–1961), and held professorships at Leiden (1966–1972), Washington (1972–1984), Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (attested 2010).

David Shulman is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1967–1971) and the University of London (~1971–1976). He spent his academic career at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1976–2016), serving as Professor of Indian Studies and Comparative Religion (~1985–1995).

David Tracy worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at Saint Joseph's Seminary (~1956–1960) and the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1960–1969), he held posts at the Catholic University of America (~1967–1969), the University of Chicago (~1985–2006), and the Committee on Social Thought (~1985–2006).

David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who completed doctoral work at Yale University (~1968–1976). He served as a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1972–2002) and held a post at Soka University of America (~2002–2004).

David W. Tien is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan (attested 2009) under James Robson and Robert H. Sharf.
David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

Dawa Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Delhi (~1970–1974) and UC Berkeley (~1976–1982), and held posts at San Francisco State University, the University of San Francisco, CIIS, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1984–2006).

Daya Ram Sahni was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Oriental College, Lahore (~1899–1903). He served as Deputy for Exploration at the Archaeological Survey of India (1931–1935) and Director of Archæology and Historical Research for Jaipur State (1935).

Dayong was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute, where he taught in 1923, under Taixu, Palden Tenzin Nyendrak, and Bai Puren, and founded the Tibetan Language School of Beijing.
Debala Mitra was an archaeologist, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Director of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1952–1983).
Debi Prasanna Pattanayak is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961) and served as director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages in 1988.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied under Surendranath Dasgupta at the University of Calcutta (~1936–1942), where he later held an academic post.
Deborah Carlson is a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. She held posts at Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology (both attested 2015).

Deborah Klimburg-Salter specializes in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Vienna (~1965–1968) and Harvard University (~1968–1976) under Oleg Grabar, later serving on the faculty at the University of Vienna (~1989–2015).
Declan Quigley is an Indologist who has held teaching positions at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei specializes in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Renmin University of China (~1995–1998) and became an associate professor of religious studies there around 1998.

Denis Twitchett was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who studied at SOAS (~1943–1944) and St Catharine's College (~1946–1950). He held professorships at the University of London (~1960–1968), Cambridge (attested 1973–1986), and Princeton (~1980–1994).

Denma Lochö Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery. He served as a Visiting Scholar at the University of Virginia (~1978–1979).
Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Vienna, earning his Magister der Philosophie under supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012).
